journal_name: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security

abstracts.abstract: The escalating sophistication of adversarial attacks on biometric systems necessitates a fundamental shift in how we model and evaluate security vulnerabilities. This paper introduces a novel information-theoretic framework for analyzing the inherent limits of template protection in biometric authentication systems. Unlike conventional approaches that focus on empirical robustness metrics, we establish theoretical bounds on the trade-off between recognition accuracy and privacy leakage using Rate-Distortion Theory. We formalize the concept of biometric information as a mutual information measure and demonstrate that previous security definitions suffer from critical inconsistencies when applied to continuous-valued biometric features. Our analysis reveals a fundamental duality between information forensics and biometric security: stronger privacy guarantees inevitably degrade authentication performance according to a precise mathematical relationship. We further prove that the optimal template protection scheme must satisfy a specific entropy conservation law, providing the first provably secure lower bound on recognition performance under privacy constraints. The theoretical framework is validated through extensive simulations on fingerprint and iris datasets, demonstrating that our derived bounds are tight and achievable. This work establishes a new paradigm for analyzing biometric security by bridging the gap between information theory and adversarial machine learning, offering fundamental insights for designing next-generation secure authentication systems.

Detecting sophisticated replay attacks on voice biometric systems remains a critical challenge in cybersecurity, as attackers increasingly employ advanced signal processing techniques to circumvent existing detection mechanisms. This paper presents an enhanced theoretical analysis of spectral characteristics that distinguish genuine human speech from replayed recordings, achieving significant improvements over prior art. We develop a novel mathematical model characterizing the acoustic distortion patterns introduced by various playback and recording devices, demonstrating that previous detection methods fail to account for the full spectrum of replay artifacts. Our analysis reveals that phase spectrum inconsistencies provide more robust indicators of replay attacks than traditionally employed magnitude spectrum features, enabling detection rates under realistic conditions. We derive closed-form expressions for the optimal detection threshold as a function of environmental noise levels and establish theoretical bounds on detection performance degradation. The proposed feature extraction method, termed Phase Coherence Analysis (PCA), reduces equal error rate by 47% compared to state-of-the-art approaches on the ASVspoof 2019 dataset. Furthermore, we prove that PCA features exhibit inherent robustness against adaptive attackers who exploit knowledge of the detection system, providing formal guarantees under a realistic adversarial model. This work offers both theoretical foundations and practical guidelines for developing replay-resilient voice biometric systems.

We present ForenChain, a novel blockchain-based distributed digital forensics framework that fundamentally reimagines evidence integrity verification in cyber-physical systems. The proposed architecture addresses critical limitations of conventional forensic approaches, including single points of failure, evidence tampering, and inadequate chain-of-custody documentation. ForenChain introduces a hierarchical sharding mechanism specifically designed for IoT environments, where massive volumes of forensic data must be processed with strict latency constraints. Our system employs a novel consensus protocol called Proof of Forensic Integrity that combines Byzantine fault tolerance with zero-knowledge proof verification, enabling efficient evidence authentication without compromising investigative confidentiality. We implement a privacy-preserving smart contract framework that automates evidence collection, timestamping, and cross-jurisdictional sharing while enforcing fine-grained access control policies. The architecture supports heterogeneous forensic analysis modules including memory forensics, network traffic analysis, and malware detection through a standardized plugin interface. Extensive evaluation on a testbed comprising 500 IoT devices demonstrates that ForenChain achieves 99.97% evidence integrity verification accuracy with a median latency of 2.3 seconds, representing a paradigm shift in scalable and trustworthy digital forensics for cyber-physical security applications.

This paper presents an enhanced steganalysis system employing deep convolutional neural networks with attention mechanisms for detecting sophisticated steganographic payloads in compressed multimedia content. While existing steganalysis methods demonstrate reasonable performance on raw images, their effectiveness degrades significantly when applied to JPEG-compressed images commonly encountered in digital forensics investigations. Our system introduces a novel frequency-domain attention module that adaptively focuses the network on steganographic artifacts in DCT coefficients while suppressing content-dependent noise. We design a multi-scale feature fusion architecture that captures both local texture irregularities and global statistical inconsistencies, addressing the fundamental challenge of detecting adaptive steganography algorithms. The training procedure incorporates a curriculum learning strategy that progressively introduces increasingly sophisticated steganographic algorithms, substantially improving generalization to unseen embedding methods. Extensive experiments on large-scale benchmarks demonstrate that our approach achieves 94.2% detection accuracy for state-of-the-art steganographic algorithms, representing a 12.4% improvement over previous CNN-based methods. Importantly, the proposed system maintains robust performance across varying JPEG quality factors and image content types. We further demonstrate practical applicability by successfully detecting steganographic content in real-world image databases used in criminal investigations, providing forensic analysts with a powerful tool for information forensics.
